title: 2 Samuel: the king and the promise
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. lines: Second Samuel tells David's reign, from the day after Saul's death to his last years.
It gives the Bible both its highest picture of a king and its most honest one. A king God chose and loved, and a book that won't hide what he did with his power.

scripture.text: And they anointed him king over Israel.

lines: It has five parts. King over Judah. The kingdom established, with Jerusalem, the ark, and the promise. David's sin and Nathan's rebuke. The troubles in David's house. And a closing collection.
Chapters eleven and twelve are the hinge.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: a crown not seized
lines: The throne comes to David without his grasping for it. He mourns Saul and Jonathan, and each man who kills a rival to win his favor is rebuked.
When the ark comes to Jerusalem, David dances with all his might before the LORD.

scripture.text: danced with all his might before the LORD

chapters.kicker: Watch for: a house for David
lines: David wants to build God a house. God turns the offer around. He will build David a house, a line of kings, with a throne established forever.
Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me.
Jews before Christ read it of a son of David to come. Christians confess it kept in Jesus. The two part over how.

scripture.text: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me

chapters.kicker: Watch for: you are that man
lines: Then the hinge. David takes Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, and has Uriah killed. The text places the whole responsibility on David, and nothing in the story blames her.
Nathan, with nothing but a word from God, names the king's crime to his face. And David confesses.
I have sinned against the LORD.

scripture.text: I have sinned against the LORD.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the sword in David's house
lines: But after it, the sword never leaves David's house. The rape of Tamar. A son murdered. Absalom's revolt. And a father weeping for the son who tried to take his throne.
The same king, the same God, and the same promise stand on both sides of chapter eleven.

scripture.text: O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!

lines: Start with chapter seven, slowly. Then chapters eleven and twelve, with Psalm fifty-one beside them.
The book gives no leader a shield against correction. Its own prophet named the king's sin.
titleCard: No leader is shielded from correction.
